newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish pound broadly unchanged in subdued trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish pound broadly unchanged in subdued trade.

text.p: The Irish pound was little changed against sterling and a shade firmer against the mark in midday trade on Thursday but dealers said activity was likely to be thin ahead of the weekend G7 meeting in Washington.
"There's not too much going on. It's quiet by yesterday's standards. Everything's fairly quiet ahead of the G7," one dealer said.
Intervention by the Irish central bank to bolster the Irish pound against sterling in recent days had left the market a little nervous, traders said.
"The market is unsure after the recent bouts of central bank intervention," one dealer said.
Traders said the Irish pound was unlikely to test 0.9500 on the downside in the short-term as sterling remained vulnerable to political factors in the run-up to the British election on May 1.
"I think we've found a bit of a bottom at 0.9500," one trader said, adding the punt could test 0.9550-0.9575 over the next few days.
By 1115 GMT, the Irish pound was at 0.9540 sterling against 0.9541 at Wednesday's close and slipped to $1.5457 from $1.5481.
It edged up to 2.6555 marks from 2.6517 as mild German inflation data weighed on the mark. West German preliminary April CPI was down 0.1 percent on the month and up 1.4 percent year-on-year.
In the ERM, the punt was trading 10.6 percent above the French franc, the weakest currency in the ERM grid.
